subject.title: [Feature]: Memory/Context Improvements (metrics + global semantic search + conversation chaining + preload on restart)

question: Should OpenClaw keep this as one memory/context umbrella, or split and sponsor narrower designs for metrics API, global recall scope, normal-session chaining, and restart preload?
rationale: The remaining work changes privacy-sensitive memory and metrics boundaries plus gateway startup behavior, and current code already has several partial mechanisms whose default policy is a maintainer product choice.

options.title: Split Into Design Tracks
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and create or confirm narrower maintainer-owned tracks for metrics/API security, session-memory graduation, conversation handoff, and restart preload policy.

options.title: Sponsor One Core RFC
options.body: Treat the bundle as one core RFC and require a single design covering privacy, permissions, defaults, migrations, and validation before any implementation PR.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Mechanisms
options.body: Close or defer broad defaults and only document the current opt-in mechanisms such as memorySearch.extraPaths, sessionMemory, QMD startup refresh, and BOOT.md.

recommendation.title: Split Into Design Tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and create or confirm narrower maintainer-owned tracks for metrics/API security, session-memory graduation, conversation handoff, and restart preload policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent cross-surface history in memory, usage, startup/QMD docs, and already provided the prior maintainer-facing review on this issue.
